verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on Friday, April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down off the coast of San Diego at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) on Friday, April 10.'; R3: 'splashdown off the coast of San Diego, expected around 5 p.m. Pacific time Friday... around 5:07 p.m.'; R4: 'splash down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026... around 8:07 p.m. ET... off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match on date, time, location, and ocean in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is returning from a 10-day moon mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission is an approximately 10-day journey around the Moon'; R2: 'The Artemis II mission began with... sending the first humans toward the Moon... historic lunar flyby'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe it as an approximately 10-day mission around the Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will begin final reentry procedures around 7:33 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'What can we expect to see during Artemis II’s return to Earth? A carefully timed sequence will guide Orion through the final stages of descent: 7:33 p.m.: Orion’s crew module will separate...'; 'Artemis II splashdown timeline A carefully timed sequence will guide Orion through the final stages of descent: 7:33 p.m.: Orion’s crew module will separate'
verifications.reasoning: 7:33 p.m. marks the start of the detailed final descent sequence with separation, directly supporting 'begin final reentry procedures around'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew module separates from the service module at 7:33 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: '7:33 p.m.: Orion’s crew module will separate from the service module'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and event match, date confirmed in context.

verifications.claim: Artemis II entry into Earth's atmosphere occurs at 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: '7:53 p.m.: When Orion reaches 400,000 feet... This moment marks the spacecraft’s first contact with the upper atmosphere'; R3: 'NASA expects reentry to begin at approximately 4:53 p.m. Pacific time' (equiv. 7:53 EDT)
verifications.reasoning: Exact time for atmospheric entry, date in context.

verifications.claim: Artemis II entry into Earth's atmosphere occurs at approximately 400,000 feet.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: '7:53 p.m.: When Orion reaches 400,000 feet above Earth’s surface... first contact with the upper atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for altitude at entry.

verifications.claim: Artemis II drogue parachutes deploy at 8:03 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: '8:03 p.m.: Around 22,000 feet in altitude, the drogue parachutes will deploy'; R3: 'Around 5:03 p.m., two small parachutes will deploy' (equiv. 8:03 EDT)

verifications.claim: Artemis II drogue parachutes deploy at approximately 22,000 feet.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: '8:03 p.m.: Around 22,000 feet in altitude, the drogue parachutes will deploy'
verifications.reasoning: Direct altitude match for drogue deployment.

verifications.claim: Artemis II main parachutes deploy at 8:04 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: '8:04 p.m.: At around 6,000 feet, the drogues will release, and the three main parachutes will deploy'; R3: 'A minute later, much larger chutes will deploy' (after 5:03, so ~5:04 PT / 8:04 EDT)

verifications.claim: Artemis II main parachutes deploy at approximately 6,000 feet.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: NASA and U.S. Navy teams will recover the Artemis II crew and the capsule following splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'teams from NASA and the U.S. military will extract the crew... Recovery teams will retrieve the crew... helicopters to the USS John P. Murtha'; R3: 'A team of Navy divers will then help... Navy helicopters will swoop in to recover them... Navy divers will then secure the capsule'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe NASA and U.S. Navy/military recovery teams for crew and capsule.
